title: KLF5-driven TAZ-FASN signaling reprograms fatty acid metabolism to support Treg differentiation in lung cancer.
authors: Huang, Hongxiang; Chen, Jinhong; Zhong, Peiyuan; Peng, Sujuan; Zhong, Qiuxa; Deng, Chenfeiyang; Wang, Fen; Lu, Zhihui; Liu, Yangyang; Chen, Li
one_liner_zh: 该文研究KLF5-TAZ-FASN轴调控肺癌脂肪酸代谢及Treg分化，虽涉及KLF5与FASN启动子结合及分子对接，但核心是肿瘤代谢与免疫，非TF-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic reprogramming is a fundamental hallmark of cancer and provides essential biochemical support for malignant progression. In lung cancer, aberrant fatty acid metabolism not only fuels cancer cell growth but also influences regulatory T cell (Treg) differentiation through altered lipid availability. Kruppel-like factor 5 (KLF5) has been implicated in lung cancer progression; however, its role in coordinating cancer fatty acid metabolism and Treg differentiation remains insufficiently defined. METHODS: We combined clinical lung cancer specimens, genetically modified lung cancer cell models, Treg differentiation systems, and mouse tumor models to define the metabolic function of KLF5. Gain- and loss-of-function approaches were used to determine how KLF5 affects lipid storage, fatty acid synthesis, extracellular free fatty acid production, and tumor growth. Conditioned-medium transfer experiments, fatty acid uptake assays, fatty acid oxidation measurements, and flow cytometry were applied to evaluate the impact of cancer cell-derived lipid output on Treg differentiation. Mechanistically, promoter-binding assays, transcriptional reporter analysis, protein-interaction experiments, molecular docking, and TAZ depletion were used to dissect how KLF5 regulates FASN-dependent fatty acid synthesis. RESULTS: KLF5 was highly expressed in lung cancer tissues and cells and showed positive associations with lipogenic markers and Treg-related indicators. Suppression of KLF5 markedly weakened the fatty acid metabolic phenotype of lung cancer cells, as reflected by reduced lipid droplet accumulation, decreased free fatty acid release, and downregulation of FASN, SCD1, DGAT2, and PLIN5. In vivo, KLF5 knockdown restrained tumor growth and reduced fatty acid synthesis-related molecular features. Mechanistically, KLF5 bound directly to the FASN promoter and cooperated with TAZ to enhance FASN transcription. KLF5 promoted nuclear accumulation of TAZ, whereas TAZ silencing attenuated KLF5-induced FASN expression, lipid accumulation, and free fatty acid production. Functionally, fatty acids released from KLF5-overexpressing lung cancer cells enhanced CD36-associated fatty acid uptake and fatty acid oxidation in Tregs, thereby promoting Treg differentiation. Conversely, KLF5 depletion reduced this lipid-associated differentiation process both in vitro and in tumor-bearing mice. CONCLUSION: This study reveals a KLF5-driven fatty acid metabolic program in lung cancer. KLF5 cooperates with TAZ to activate FASN transcription, thereby increasing lipogenesis and free fatty acid release. The resulting lipid output promotes CD36-dependent fatty acid uptake and oxidation in Tregs and supports their differentiation. These findings identify the KLF5-TAZ-FASN axis as a cancer metabolism-centered mechanism linking lung cancer lipogenesis to Treg differentiation, highlighting this pathway as a potential metabolic vulnerability for interfering with fatty acid-supported lung cancer progression.
abstract_zh: 背景：代谢重编程是癌症的基本标志，为恶性进展提供必要的生化支持。在肺癌中，异常的脂肪酸代谢不仅促进癌细胞生长，还通过改变脂质可用性影响调节性T细胞（Treg）分化。Kruppel样因子5（KLF5）已被涉及在肺癌进展中；然而，其在协调癌症脂肪酸代谢和Treg分化中的作用仍未被充分定义。方法：我们结合临床肺癌标本、基因修饰的肺癌细胞模型、Treg分化系统和小鼠肿瘤模型，以定义KLF5的代谢功能。使用功能获得和功能丧失方法来确定KLF5如何影响脂质储存、脂肪酸合成、细胞外游离脂肪酸产生和肿瘤生长。应用条件培养基转移实验、脂肪酸摄取测定、脂肪酸氧化测量和流式细胞术，评估癌细胞来源的脂质输出对Treg分化的影响。机制上，使用启动子结合测定、转录报告分析、蛋白质相互作用实验、分子对接和TAZ耗竭，来解析KLF5如何调控FASN依赖性脂肪酸合成。结果：KLF5在肺癌组织和细胞中高表达，并与脂肪生成标志物和Treg相关指标呈正相关。抑制KLF5显著削弱了肺癌细胞的脂肪酸代谢表型，表现为脂滴积累减少、游离脂肪酸释放降低，以及FASN、SCD1、DGAT2和PLIN5下调。在体内，KLF5敲低抑制了肿瘤生长，并减少了脂肪酸合成相关的分子特征。机制上，KLF5直接结合FASN启动子，并与TAZ协同增强FASN转录。KLF5促进TAZ的核积累，而TAZ沉默减弱了KLF5诱导的FASN表达、脂质积累和游离脂肪酸产生。功能上，KLF5过表达肺癌细胞释放的脂肪酸增强了Treg中CD36相关的脂肪酸摄取和脂肪酸氧化，从而促进Treg分化。相反，KLF5耗竭在体外和荷瘤小鼠中均减少了这种脂质相关的分化过程。结论：本研究揭示了肺癌中KLF5驱动的脂肪酸代谢程序。KLF5与TAZ协同激活FASN转录，从而增加脂肪生成和游离脂肪酸释放。由此产生的脂质输出促进Treg中CD36依赖性脂肪酸摄取和氧化，并支持其分化。这些发现将KLF5-TAZ-FASN轴确定为以癌症代谢为中心的机制，连接肺癌脂肪生成与Treg分化，突出该通路作为干扰脂肪酸支持的肺癌进展的潜在代谢脆弱点。
